A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the molecular recognition of microbial lipid antigens by T cell receptors (TCRs) is highly specific and involves the recognition of both the lipid antigen and the CD1 molecule.
microbial lipid-based antigends are presented by CD1 molecules and recognized by T cells in a similar fashion to that of the recognition of peptidic self- and pathogen-derived antigens.
T cells recognize microbial lipid-based antigins in a manner analogous to that of the recognition by T cells to peptide antigens.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the recognition of lipid-based antigens involves a combination of T cell receptor recognition of lipid-based peptide-MHC complexes and lipid-specific recognition by the T cell.

T cell immunity to microbial lipids is highly complex and that T cell responses to these antigens are likely shaped by the combined effects of the lipid antigen structure, its CD1-presenting molecule and the T cell antigen receptor.

the structural and chemical features of the CD1-lipid complexes are key to determine the molecular interactions with the T cell antigen receptors, which ultimately dictate the T cell activation and the ensuing immune response.
